MUTATIONS: the write scope takes a bit of its own, so the write grant holds core and write and the read grant never holds write; a shared bit would erase the line between the read and write grants (SPEC-369 A5)
the write scope is named write, so a grant's scope names say which grant changes data; a reader would see the law track's name on the write grant (SPEC-369 A1)
every scope, write included, is listed once, so a grant's names show the write scope it holds; a reader would lose the write grant's write (SPEC-369 A1)
the core credential's grant is the read grant, core alone; with write it would let the read token reach every write tool (SPEC-369 A5)
the write credential grants core and write; core alone would leave no token able to reach a write tool (SPEC-369 A1)
the write credential's id is mcp-write-token, the name it is provisioned under; another id would load nothing and grant no write, with no refusal to say so (SPEC-369 A1)
a write credential holding the core or law-track credential's value refuses start, compared in constant time; without it one token would hold both grants' scopes (SPEC-369 A4)
